question.text: An automobile travelling with speed of $60 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}$, can brake to stop within a distance of $20 \mathrm{~cm}$. If the car is going twice as fast, i.e $120 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}$, the stopping distance will be

solution.text: If the initial speed is doubled, the stopping distance becomes four times, i.e. $80 \mathrm{~m}$.
